resources.string: TapLock requires Device Administrator authorization solely to use the Force Lock policy to turn off and lock your screen on demand.
TapLock requires Device Administrator privileges solely to lock your screen on demand using the Force lock policy.
Before you can lock your screen from the home screen icon or widget, TapLock needs one-time Device Administrator activation.
Device Administrator permission is active. You can now lock your screen on demand.
Android protects system lock functions. TapLock uses Android\'s native Device Administration API with strictly the single \"Force lock\" policy. Unlike other screen lock apps, TapLock requires:
Pin Lock Shortcut to Home Screen

This will revoke TapLock\'s screen lock privilege. You will need to reactivate it before you can lock the screen again.\n\nNote: Android requires deactivating device administrator apps before they can be uninstalled.
Lock shortcut added to Home screen
Launcher does not support direct pinning. Long-press the TapLock app icon to drag the shortcut to your Home screen.

For your phone to require authentication (PIN, pattern, password, or biometrics) upon wake, ensure a secure lock screen is enabled in your phone\'s Settings > Lock screen.\n\nIf your phone is set to \"Swipe\" or \"None\", TapLock will turn off the screen, but it will not require authentication to reopen.
Device Administrator permission is not active. Please tap \"Activate Device Administrator\" first.
SecurityException: Unable to lock screen. Please ensure Device Administrator is active.
One-tap screen lock button for your Home screen.
Add a 1-tap lock control to your Samsung Home screen via Widget or App Shortcut.
